text:
- chief complaint: the patient reports intermittent mid-abdominal pain for about two years, with alternating constipation and diarrhea, referred for abdominal pain and diarrhea.
- history of present illness: the patient has had intermittent periumbilical pain for about two years, with recent months of alternating constipation (3-4 bowel movements weekly, hard stools) and occasional one-time diarrhea triggered by creamy foods. A recent ER CT was normal. Past history includes GERD, anxiety, and depression. Recent labs showed mildly elevated ALT and AST. No bleeding, nausea, vomiting, weight loss, or jaundice. Alcohol use is limited to occasional beer; no drug use.
- physical examination: bowel sounds present in all quadrants; mild left periumbilical tenderness; stool palpable in lower colon; mildly enlarged liver (hepatomegaly); no jaundice; clear lungs; normal heart sounds.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: intermittent abdominal pain, constipation, occasional diarrhea, sensitive stomach.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: fiber supplement started (dosage N/A); discussion of switching from Crestor (rosuvastatin), to be coordinated with primary care.
- follow-up instructions: liver ultrasound within two weeks; repeat liver enzyme and other labs today; return visit in four weeks; avoid alcohol; drink at least 48 ounces of water daily; avoid trigger foods; call primary care about Crestor.
